# Module reference

<!-- Generated by tests/support/gen-module-reference. Do not edit by hand: change the
     module's module.conf or files, then run tests/support/gen-module-reference. -->

This page lists the 47 public modules in `modules/`. It is generated from each
module's `module.conf` and file layout, and `tests/check` fails when it is out of date.

- Turn a module off with `marksharc module disable <name>`, or see
  [choosing modules](USERGUIDE.md#choosing-modules).
- Set an option with a `set <module>.<key> <value>` line in your overlay's `config.conf`.
  [CONFIGURATION.md](CONFIGURATION.md) describes the file format and the settings that
  belong to the core, not to a module.

How to read an entry:

- **Order** is the load position (0–99). Lower numbers load first; ties load by name.
- **Native code** names the shells the module has its own files for. Lines declared in
  `module.conf` and executables in `bin/` work in every shell, so a module with no native
  code for a shell can still contribute there. [fish.md](fish.md) has the Fish parity table.
- **Requires** lists commands that must be installed, or the operating system the module
  is limited to. A module whose requirement is not met skips itself silently.
- **Installers** run with `marksharc install <name>`; **update steps** run with
  `marksharc update` and can be selected with `--only <label>`.

## Modules

### `agent`

Agent-session markers: the option that extends the session classifier's marker list

- **Order:** 20
- **Native code:** zsh

| Option | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `agent.markers` | *(empty)* | Space-separated environment variable names that indicate an agent session; replaces the core default list (set agent.markers in config.conf) |
| `agent.bash_env` | `off` | Export the MarkSharc Bash startup hook for noninteractive Bash children |

### `brew`

Homebrew: PATH directories (env) and cached shellenv (init)

- **Order:** 10
- **Native code:** zsh, bash, fish
- **Shell functions:** `setup-homebrew` (zsh, bash, fish)
- **Update steps:** `brew-update` (`brew update`), `brew-upgrade` (`brew upgrade`)

| Option | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `brew.linuxbrew_tier` | `local` | PATH tier for Linuxbrew (local keeps the old order; brew puts it ahead of the system tier) |

Declared in `module.conf`:

```text
path brew /opt/homebrew/bin
path brew /opt/homebrew/sbin
path ${_ms_opt_brew_linuxbrew_tier} /home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin
path ${_ms_opt_brew_linuxbrew_tier} /home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/sbin
```

### `bun`

Bun JavaScript runtime: BUN_INSTALL, user-tier path, completion

- **Order:** 40
- **Native code:** zsh

Declared in `module.conf`:

```text
env BUN_INSTALL ~/.bun when dir ~/.bun
path user ~/.bun/bin when dir ~/.bun/bin
```

### `completion-carapace`

- **Order:** 72
- **Native code:** zsh
- **Requires:** command `carapace`

| Option | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `completion-carapace.enable` | `off` | Activate Carapace completion in interactive zsh and Bash shells |
| `completion-carapace.bridges` | `zsh,fish,bash` | Bridged completion engines for CARAPACE_BRIDGES (comma or space separated; empty or off disables) |
| `completion-carapace.excludes` | *(empty)* | Commands excluded from Carapace via CARAPACE_EXCLUDES (comma or space separated) |
| `completion-carapace.allow_fzf_tab` | `off` | Keep completion-fzf-tab active alongside Carapace (not recommended; known upstream conflicts) |

### `cuda`

NVIDIA CUDA: MPS variables and /usr/local/cuda/bin (Linux)

- **Order:** 42
- **Native code:** none (declarative only)
- **Requires:** os linux

Declared in `module.conf`:

```text
env CUDA_MPS_PIPE_DIRECTORY /tmp/nvidia-mps when file /dev/nvidiactl
env CUDA_MPS_LOG_DIRECTORY ~/tmp/nvidia-mps when file /dev/nvidiactl
path app /usr/local/cuda/bin when file /dev/nvidiactl
```

### `ls`

ls family: ll la dir lf lsf (eza when installed)

- **Order:** 23
- **Native code:** zsh, bash
- **Packages:** brew `eza`

Declared in `module.conf`:

```text
alias dir "ls -l"
alias lsf "ls -F"
alias la "ls -a"
alias lf "ls -FA"
alias ll "ls -lA"
alias dir "eza -l" when command eza
alias lsf "eza -F" when command eza
alias la "eza -a" when command eza
alias lf "eza -FA" when command eza
alias ll "eza -lA" when command eza
```
